items.summary_1line: KV cache compression is critical for large reasoning models, where most of the cost comes from long generated reasoning traces rather than the input prompt. These traces often contain redundant and low-utility tokens...

items.summary_1line: TideCache is a serving system for hybrid LLMs on CPU-GPU superchips that reallocates GPU memory among cache types and streams KV prefixes layer by layer, implemented in SGLang and tested on GB300 and GH200.

items.summary_1line: Proposes LS-MBPO, a lightweight residual reinforcement learning framework that uses latent world models instead of large image or video generators to improve pretrained vision-language-action robot policies, tested on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and a real ALOHA robot.

items.title: Abstract What Varies, Reuse Longer Patterns: Efficient Offline Chain-of-Thought Compression
items.summary_1line: CRAFT is an offline method that abstracts problem-specific details into slots, compresses shared expression templates once, and applies the edits to build shorter chain-of-thought training targets, cutting compressor budget by a median 90.7%.
items.editor_note: Output-side reduction: builds shorter chain-of-thought training targets, cutting compressor budget by a median 90.7%.

items.title: DKnown-Jev-2: Article-Level Answer-Evidence Classification and Efficient Inference with a Pre-trained Language Model
items.summary_1line: DKnown-Jev-2 is an article-level classifier that labels whether a candidate article holds answer evidence for a normative question, reporting 91.77% accuracy and 91.28% macro-F1 on a 972-instance test set, 2.16 and 2.37 points above Jev.
items.editor_note: Off-thread: an answer-evidence classifier that mentions efficient inference only in passing.

items.title: Announcing vLLM-GR: Efficient Inference for Generative Recommendation
items.summary_1line: vLLM-GR is an open-source inference and serving framework built on vLLM that adds beam search over semantic item IDs to generate candidate sets for recommendation models such as OneRec.
items.editor_note: Latest item: vLLM's own extension into generative recommendation serving.

editorial.tldr: This is a loose theme thread, not one event: 22 independent items from Nov 6 to Nov 24 that each cut inference or agent cost at a different layer, mostly arXiv papers plus posts from Google, Baseten, Microsoft Research, UW, AWS and vLLM. Through Nov 19 the KV cache was the most-attacked target, ending with RoCoKV and TideCache.
editorial.whats_new: vLLM shipped vLLM-GR on Nov 24, an open-source serving framework that adds beam search over semantic item IDs so generative recommendation models such as OneRec can run on the vLLM stack.
editorial.why_it_matters: KV-cache memory is still the most-attacked bottleneck here (6 of 22 items), and vLLM-GR shows mainstream serving engines now stretching to non-chat workloads, so one serving stack may soon cover both LLM and recommendation traffic.
editorial.take_for_builders: If long-context or reasoning workloads are memory-bound, profile KV-cache size per request before buying GPUs; if you run generative recommendation on a separate stack, test vLLM-GR before building custom beam-search serving.

beats.headline: Serving stacks: XLA Serving Engine, edge simulation, cross-Region routing
beats.summary: Infrastructure that decides where and on what hardware requests run.

beats.headline: Cheaper decoding: draft pruning, diffusion blocks, MoE traffic, small models
beats.summary: Efficiency inside the model and decode loop: cheaper draft verification, overlapping diffusion blocks, less all-to-all traffic, quantization and a 4GB agent model.

beats.headline: Shrink what the model reads and writes: images, audio, chain-of-thought
beats.summary: Token reduction on input (VLM cropping, chunked long-audio ASR) and on output (shorter chain-of-thought training targets).

beats.headline: Agent-level efficiency: coordinated delegation and learned token budgets
beats.summary: Cost cuts at the agent layer rather than the serving stack.

beats.headline: The KV cache becomes the main target
beats.summary: Six papers attack cache memory: intent-aware prefix reuse, verified compression, prefill/decode KV translation, Gemma 4 shared K=V storage, reasoning-trace compression, and hybrid-model cache streaming in SGLang.

beats.headline: Keyword matches outside LLM serving
beats.summary: Two papers share the word "efficient" but address robot-policy RL training and an answer-evidence classifier, not inference serving.

beats.headline: vLLM extends to generative recommendation with vLLM-GR
beats.summary: A mainstream serving engine adds a non-chat decoding mode: beam search over semantic item IDs.
